entries.b8db8ba7b3acd9a3: This category covers the planning and sale of travel using air transport, system development and operation, and others, carried out by JALPAK Co., Ltd., JAL Digital Co., Ltd. and others. In the segment information notes, it is presented as “Other,” separate from the total of reportable segments, and includes travel business and others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥227,477 million (¥224,125 million in the previous fiscal year). In ground-handling services contracted from foreign airlines, it began commercial use of towing tractors compatible with Level 4 autonomous driving (fully unmanned operation under specific conditions) at Haneda Airport and Narita International Airport from December 2025. Because it is not a reportable segment, it is placed last rather than in order of external revenue.

entries.be6b367406ef28ed: This reportable segment is centered on mileage services for member customers. The operation of the mileage program, the credit card business, the wholesale business and others are carried out by JAL Mileage Bank Co., Ltd., JALCARD Co., Ltd., JALUX Co., Ltd. and others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥148,210 million (¥131,779 million in the previous fiscal year), making it the second-largest category among reportable segments. Revenue before elimination of intersegment transactions rose 10.9% year on year, against a background of higher revenue at JALUX and an increase in the number of miles issued. Under the “JAL Mileage Bank” member mileage program, miles are granted according to the use of passenger transport services and other services; the portion of granted miles expected to be used in the future is recorded as contract liabilities and recognized as revenue as the miles are used. In February 2026, equity-method affiliate MoneySquare HD Co., Ltd. launched a new program that allows miles to be accumulated through daily asset management. To extend mile services to overseas customers, it has also formed partnerships with overseas financial service providers such as Capital One and Bilt Rewards.
entries.bfc31168e7a649cb: Profit attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥137.6 billion (up 28.6% year on year). The company cites as factors in its results the growth of international passenger business, which was strong, and of domestic passenger business, where demand stimulation measures were effective, as well as the growth of the high-profit Mile / Finance and Commerce Business. On the expense side, fuel costs increased due to higher usage, and personnel costs increased due to increased investment in human capital; however, the company states that it kept costs down despite the progress of the weaker yen, thereby restraining the increase in expenses. Major expenses are fuel costs, airport facility usage fees, maintenance costs, aircraft sales commissions, aircraft-related costs (depreciation, leases and insurance related to aircraft), service costs and personnel costs. In the Mile / Finance and Commerce Business, higher revenue at JALUX and an increase in the number of miles issued led to stable performance.
entries.c1f50b1efbe8cb65: This reportable segment, the core of the Japan Airlines Group, transports passengers, cargo, mail and baggage on international and domestic routes.
entries.c6dc7c563c47797c: This is passenger, cargo and mail transport on international routes operated by Japan Airlines Co., Ltd. and Japan Transocean Air Co., Ltd. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, paid passenger numbers were 8,008,848 (105.6% year on year), the paid seat load factor was 85.8%, and paid cargo ton-kilometers were 3,220,293 thousand ton-kilometers (116.4% year on year). Revenue from international routes before elimination of intersegment transactions was 110.6% of the prior-year period, with passenger revenue at 109.1% and cargo and mail revenue at 118.7%. In January 2026, it launched the Narita–Delhi route and operated Airbus A350-1000 aircraft, the latest equipment, daily on 12 flights across five routes, including the Haneda–Paris route. In February 2026, Japan Transocean Air Co., Ltd. began service on the Okinawa–Taipei route. When foreign airlines suspended services in the Middle East in March 2026 due to the deterioration of the situation there, it captured substitute demand for direct flights on European routes and connecting demand for North America-bound flights from India, securing revenue exceeding that of the suspended Doha route. In international cargo, it captured Asia–North America demand with scheduled cargo flights on US routes using its own freighters and large freighters of Kalitta Air, and strengthened high-value cargo such as pharmaceuticals and AI and EV-related parts.

entries.cb6a11397aa17b58: This is a medium- and long-haul international LCC operated by ZIPAIR Tokyo Co., Ltd. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it added flights on the Narita–Bangkok and Seoul routes and on the Los Angeles and Honolulu routes. Paid passenger numbers were 1,380,861 (101.8% year on year), available seat-kilometers increased to 115.7% of the prior-year level, and the paid seat load factor was 77.7% (84.8% in the previous fiscal year). From February 2026, it became the first Asian airline to install the satellite internet service “Starlink,” and it has gradually increased the number of equipped flights toward offering the service on all aircraft and routes.
entries.cfc51c9b90a19e24: On international routes, in addition to passenger demand from strong inbound travel, business demand passengers departing from Japan recovered beyond plan. On domestic routes, the company stimulated demand through various campaigns, and used the Osaka-Kansai Expo as an opportunity to encourage inbound visitors to travel around regional areas. By region, revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥994,113 million in Japan, ¥369,500 million in Asia and Oceania, ¥498,820 million in the Americas, and ¥150,080 million in Europe. In cargo, the company is strengthening its acquisition of high-value cargo, such as pharmaceuticals and AI and EV-related parts. Miles are a service for members, and the company is expanding the occasions for earning and using miles through partnerships with cross-industry partners in Japan and overseas, and with financial businesses such as Capital One and Bilt Rewards overseas. Separately, there is contract handling for foreign airlines, in which the company is entrusted by other airlines with airport ground handling. No specific customer accounts for 10% or more of consolidated revenue.

entries.e6d5b763a947419e: Consolidated operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,012,515 million (¥2.0125 trillion, up 9.1% year on year). External revenue was ¥1,535,525 million for the Full-Service Carrier Business (¥1,396,294 million in the previous year), accounting for approximately 76%; ¥227,477 million for "Other" (¥224,125 million in the previous year); ¥148,210 million for the Mile / Finance and Commerce Business (¥131,779 million in the previous year); and ¥101,302 million for the LCC Business (¥91,895 million in the previous year). International passenger revenue (Full-Service Carrier) increased by ¥63.5 billion year on year, and domestic passenger revenue (same) increased by ¥37.5 billion. Revenue related to air transport is recognized upon completion of the air transport service. For air tickets not expected to be used for air transport (unused tickets expected to expire), the timing of recognition is estimated by considering the conditions of the tickets and past trends. Miles are granted according to the use of passenger transport services and other services, and the portion expected to be used in the future is recorded as contract liabilities and recognized as revenue as they are used.

entries.f54b903ece871ae3: This reportable segment, the core of the Japan Airlines Group, transports passengers, cargo, mail and baggage on international and domestic routes. Air transport services connecting the world and Japan, and cities and regions, and cargo and mail services combining cargo space on its own passenger aircraft with dedicated cargo aircraft, are provided by the company as well as J-Air Co., Ltd., Japan Air Commuter Co., Ltd., Hokkaido Air System Co., Ltd., Japan Transocean Air Co., Ltd., Ryukyu Air Commuter Co., Ltd. and others. External revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,535,525 million (¥1,396,294 million in the previous fiscal year), accounting for about 76% of consolidated revenue of ¥2,012,515 million and making it the largest category. Revenue before elimination of intersegment transactions rose 9.3% year on year; in international passenger services, robust inbound demand and business demand originating in Japan recovered above plan, and in domestic passenger services, various campaigns stimulated demand, which led to higher revenue. Paid passenger numbers on international and domestic routes combined were 46,242,888 (105.8% of the prior-year period), and the paid seat load factor was 85.1%. The nine airline companies in the group, including the company, hold business permits from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism as domestic air transport operators under the Civil Aeronautics Act, and the validity period of these permits is not stipulated by laws or regulations.
